summary: Saved drilldown tracehook parameters stripped during dashboard snapshot export with PII redaction
description:
Issue summary: Customer exports a dashboard snapshot with the org-level 'Redact PII' option enabled. Drilldown links on that snapshot that normally include tracehook query parameters (trace_id, trace_ts, org_id) are stripped or URL-encoded into a single param key during export. When users click the trace link from the exported snapshot, the console returns a 404 or a 'trace not found' message once the retention compaction job runs.

Impact: Several reporting teams at Acme Analytics cannot link back from historical snapshots to associated traces; this breaks audit workflows and slows investigations. Customer reported it for 4 snapshots across 2 dashboards.

Environment: prod (us-east), affected org id: 15892, UI version: console@2026.03.07, backend services: export-service v3.8.1, tracehook-proxy v2.5.0.

Steps to reproduce:
1) In prod org 15892, open a dashboard with drilldown link configured to include tracehook params (trace_id, trace_ts).
2) Enable org-level 'Redact PII' in Console settings (customer setting - redaction: true).
3) Click 'Export snapshot' -> choose 'Include drilldowns' -> export.
4) Open exported snapshot (downloaded HTML) and click a saved drilldown link; observe URL parameters.
5) After background retention compaction (or simulate by hitting retention compact endpoint), click link again or follow link from a snapshot older than retention boundary.

Expected behavior: Exported snapshot should preserve the tracehook namespace and its trace_id/trace_ts values (or include a signed proxy link) so that clicking a drilldown opens the correct trace in Console even after retention compaction. Redaction should not strip structured tracehook query keys required for link resolution.

Observed behavior: Tracehook parameters are either removed entirely or collapsed into a single encoded param (e.g. _redacted=tracehook%3Atrace_id%3D...); console's trace resolution rejects these and returns 404. Behavior is intermittent depending on snapshot age and whether retention compaction has run.

Attachments/links: Snapshot files provided by customer: snap-15892-20260215-1.html, snap-15892-20260222-2.html. Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/support/archives/C03ABC123/p1644123456789. Grafana dashboard showing retention compaction run times: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/retention/compaction-runs
comments: 2026-03-13 09:12 - Asha Patel (Support): Contacted customer and requested exported snapshot HTML and the dashboard id. Customer uploaded snap-15892-20260215-1.html and snap-15892-20260222-2.html. Noted that redaction is org-wide and they cannot disable it. SLA P1 noted.

2026-03-13 11:05 - Miguel Torres (Oncall Eng): Reproduced locally by toggling redaction on staging. Confirmed that export-service v3.8.1 calls redaction pipeline which currently runs a URL param sanitizer that flattens unknown query namespaces. Created internal repro and attached logs.

2026-03-13 14:48 - SRE (Priya Nair): Observed that retention compaction rewrites trace lookup store keys. If query params are URL-encoded into a single key, the trace-lookup service cannot map to trace index after compaction. Suspect export pipeline and redaction sanitizer interact poorly.

2026-03-14 08:23 - Miguel Torres (Oncall Eng): Created internal follow-up INT-331210 to track console export-service fix and assigned to export-service owner. Proposed interim workaround for customer (below).

2026-03-14 10:59 - Asha Patel (Support): Customer confirmed workaround temporarily works for 2 of 4 snapshots. Requested estimate for permanent fix and whether data recovery is possible for older snapshots.
investigation_notes: Repro steps executed on staging with console@2026.03.07 + export-service v3.8.1. Observed that 'redaction' transformation includes a generic URLParamScrubber that collapses unknown query namespaces into _redacted param when outputting static snapshot HTML.
tracehook-proxy expects query keys in namespace 'th:' (e.g., th:trace_id) or plain trace_id depending on legacy config. Redaction scrubber does not whitelist 'th:' namespace leading to collapse.

Retention compaction changes the trace index keyspace (compacted index uses short-hash prefix). If lookup URL is already malformed, compaction makes it irreversible from the malformed URL. This explains 404s appearing only after compaction runs.

Reviewed code in export-service URL sanitizer: function sanitizeUrlParams(redactionRules, url) -> uses URLSearchParams except it normalizes by encoding ':' which later becomes part of single param. Found missing allowlist for 'th' and 'trace_id' keys.
resolution_notes: Workaround provided (2026-03-13): Instructed customer to re-export with 'Include drilldowns' and temporarily disable org-level 'Redact PII' for snapshot exports. Alternative: use the 'Share link (signed)' workflow which generates a signed redirect that preserves tracehook resolution without exposing raw params. Provided step-by-step guide in support reply.

Permanent fix (planned): export-service change to whitelist tracehook-related query keys (th:trace_id, trace_id, trace_ts, org_id) and to emit signed proxy links for any tracehook parameter when redaction is enabled. Patch PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/87421. Internal ticket INT-331210 tracks rollout to prod and publishes regression test cases.

Recovery for existing malformed snapshots: partial. For snapshots where params collapsed, we can attempt a server-side postprocessor that decodes _redacted payload and rewrites links to signed proxy links if source trace ids can be recovered. This process is manual and has been offered as professional-services work for Acme Analytics; needs sign-off.

Next steps: 1) Merge PR and run canary in staging (owner: export-service team). 2) Add unit/integration tests for snapshot export with redaction enabled. 3) Add monitoring alert for exported snapshot link error rate (trace link 404s). 4) Follow up with customer to schedule re-export or enable signed-link proxy for historical snapshots.
Estimated timeline: patch ready and code review in progress; canary deployment estimate 3 business days after approval.
